svg.title: How the text of an issue and its comments reaches the AI
svg.desc: Each text of the issue and its comments loses its HTML, as GitHub hides it, and what GitHub doesn't show of its tables, fences, drawings and math, read from the same text: the cells beyond the header of a table, the words of the row that opens fenced code but a plain name of a language, the source of a diagram, a map or a 3D model and math that can hide text, each with a note in its place, and the title of a link or an image, which the page shows only on hover, with nothing in its place. Then it loses its link reference definitions and footnotes without a reference, which GitHub shows as nothing as well, each with a note in its place, then the characters that GitHub shows as nothing and, outside code, their character references, which GitHub reads as the characters, and is cut off after 20,000 characters. In this order, no invisible character or reference can end an HTML comment that GitHub never ends. It goes into a code fence with one backtick more than its longest run of backticks, so that no line of the text can end it. The heading above the fence, which only the script writes, names the author, the role and the date. The other issues and discussions become excerpts without HTML, table cells, drawings, math, titles and definitions alike, lose their invisible characters and the references of them too and go into JSON. The titles of the issues that a maintainer corrected lose their invisible characters and the references of them as well and reach corrections.md as JSON strings in a code fence that no title can close. A notice in the log counts the definitions, the parts of tables, drawings and math, the titles and the characters that were removed.
